Read the following text carefully and answer the question no. 4 and 5 : Topic : Maxim Gorky  Maxim Gorky was born on March 16, 1868, in the Volga River city of Nizhny Novgorod, Russia’s fourth largest city. Gorky lost his father when he was 4 years old and mother at the age of 11. He was brought up by his maternal grandparents. Gorky’s grandmother had a fondness for literature and compassion for the poor. He left home at the age of 12 and began a series of occupations, as an errand boy, a dish washer on a steamer, and apprentice to an icon maker. He wandered widely about Russia, the Ukraine, and the Caucasus for six years. Gorky began writing under pseudonym (Jehudiel Khlamida). publishing stories and articles in newspapers of the Volga region. He began using the pseudonym Gorky (literally ’’bitter") in 1892, while working for the Tiflis newspaper (The Caucasus). Gorky's first book, a two-volume collection of his writings entitled (Essays and Stories) was published in 1898. After the publication of his world famous novel ‘Mother’ in 1906 his reputation increased rapidly. From 1906 to 1913, Gorky lived on the island of Capri in southern Italy, partly for health reasons and partly to escape the increasingly repressive atmosphere in Russia. He was awarded 'Griboyedov’ prize in 1903. This great man breathed his last on 18 June 1936 in Moscow, Russia.

Read the following text carefully and answer the question no. 4 and 5 : Topic : Stephen Hawking  Stephen Hawking is considered the greatest physicist after Einstein. He was born in England in 1942. He was very skilled in Mathematics from the early age. He married at the age of 21. He wrote the book ‘A Brief History of Time : From the Big Bang to the Present Times’ in 1988. In this book he explains cosmology for the general public. It became famous and established his reputation as a great scientist. He received his Ph.D in cosmology from Cambridge University when he was only 26. But fortune did not favour him. In 1972 he became a victim of Gehrig's disease. Since then, he has been confined to a wheel- chair with no power to control his body. But he continue teaching through the help of computer. In 1974, he won the prestigious Albert Einstein award for theoretical physics. In 1979, he joined Cambridge University as Lucasian Professor of Mathematics. He carried out his research work using his computes. The great scientist breathed his last on 14 March 2018.
